clue.text: One in transition might acquire this derivatives house

definitions.text: One in transition might acquire this
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read with a different break: someone changing gender has a coming operation still ahead of them
second meaning: a market where contracts for later delivery are traded

explanation.surface: A financial firm specialising in derivatives is up for sale while it changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer differently and it reads FUTURE SEX CHANGE: something a person in gender transition may undergo. 'Transition' looks like a corporate takeover but is the personal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Futures are a main class of derivatives, and an exchange is the house or market where such contracts are traded.

clue.text: Say "Lay on, Macduff …!" after James for one brandished sword

parts.note: the bandleader James Last is one well-known bearer of that surname

indicators.note: a weapon that is brandished is waved about wildly, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A quotation from Macbeth's final fight, with Macbeth waving his sword at Macduff.
explanation.walkthrough: James Last was a German bandleader, so James is a famous Last. 'Lay on, Macduff' is what Macbeth says just before he is killed, an example of the answer, hence 'Say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth speaks this line before his death in the play, so it is a well-known example of a character's final utterance, often quoted ironically.

clue.text: Port? Foreign attaché knocked back bottles!

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is tipped backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction
to bottle something is to keep it shut inside, so the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: the end of the French-looking word and the start of the other, read as a run of letters

explanation.surface: A diplomat abroad downs a lot of bottles of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink to go with 'knocked back bottles', but it is a harbour town; the answer runs backwards across 'Foreign attaché'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a major Moroccan seaport on the Strait of Gibraltar, so it fits a definition naming a harbour city.

clue.text: Siblings skinned gammon in S Yorks town

indicators.note: skinning removes the outer layer, so the first and last letters are stripped away

parts.note: BROTHERS without its outside letters
gammon is cured ham

explanation.surface: Brothers preparing a joint of gammon in a South Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinned' sounds like a butcher's job on the gammon, but it applies to the siblings. S Yorks is South Yorkshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotherham is a large market town in South Yorkshire, England, near Sheffield.

clue.text: Quiet book missing a fragment

parts.note: the sound made to ask for quiet

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: a book can be called a good read
the letter to remove

explanation.surface: A hushed library book is missing a torn-out piece.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'read' is a noun for something to read, as in 'a gripping read'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a small scrap or torn strip of something, a close synonym for a broken-off piece.

clue.text: Instrument unknown characters cut and polish

parts.note: x and y are the usual unknowns in algebra
to lop is to cut off
to hone is to sharpen or refine

explanation.surface: Mysterious people trimming and buffing a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people but means letters; mathematicians use the last letters of the alphabet for unknown quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: A xylophone is a percussion instrument of wooden bars struck with mallets.

clue.text: Hospital on Iona raised capital

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something up turns it to read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Money was raised for a hospital on the Scottish island of Iona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised capital' reads as fundraising, but 'capital' is a city. Iona is a small Hebridean island off Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Game to be arranged, Gwyn admits

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Nell Gwyn was the actress and mistress of Charles II
the standard abbreviation for to be arranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Gwyn concedes that a match is still to be scheduled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' tempts as an anagram signal, but the whole phrase is the abbreviation. Nell Gwyn was a famous 17th-century English actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team ball game, popular in Britain and the Commonwealth, where players shoot into a high hoop.

clue.text: Sober geezer, once drunk, a reformed character?

indicators.note: someone drunk is muddled and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sober man who used to drink: a reformed character indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's reform is from drinking; the answer's reform is from meanness, after the ghosts visit him in Dickens's A Christmas Carol. A geezer is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's miser ends A Christmas Carol transformed into a generous man, so he is literally a fictional figure who changed his ways.

clue.text: Screen vehicle going round the outskirts of Nairobi

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: motor is a word for a car

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a place, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the Kenyan capital

explanation.surface: A car drives around the edge of Nairobi, perhaps on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' looks like a verb about vetting, but it is the computer display.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor is the display unit of a computer, the screen that shows its output.

clue.text: Crescent-shaped string instrument imported clear of tax

indicators.note: goods imported are brought in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a lute is a plucked string instrument
a net amount is what remains after tax

explanation.surface: A crescent-shaped stringed instrument brought into the country without paying duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear of tax' sounds like duty-free importing, but it is a financial term for an amount after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a half-moon shaped space or window in architecture, so the word works adjectivally for something crescent-like.

clue.text: Join a union

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bring or come together
second meaning: the name of a large British trade union

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to sign up to a trade union; the name of one big British union is itself the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to combine into one, and Unite is the name of Britain's largest private-sector labour organisation.

clue.text: Double assignation involving uniform constable (about 51)

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the outer piece holds the others
something about another lies around it, so one piece is wrapped round the number

parts.note: an assignation is a romantic meeting
Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet
Police Constable
51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A romantic meeting with a uniformed police officer of about fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' looks like a modifier on the date, but it is the definition. PC is the British abbreviation for a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A duplicate is an exact copy, so it means a double or twin of an original.

clue.text: Somewhat slow husband seen in broad Stetson periodically

indicators.note: something seen within another sits inside it, so one piece is placed within

parts.note: broad means large or wide
the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A slow-moving husband wearing a wide cowboy hat every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad Stetson' looks like a hat description, but the adjective joins the container and the hat supplies only its even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Larghetto is the musical tempo marking meaning fairly slow, a little quicker than largo.

clue.text: Actor Spall taking year off after getting stung by German insect

indicators.note: a sting pierces the skin, so one piece is driven into the other
taking something off removes it, so the named letter goes

parts.note: Timothy Spall is an English actor
Y is the abbreviation for year
GER is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: An actor takes a gap year and is then stung by an insect in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect' seems to be what stings him, but it is the definition; the sting is the German abbreviation going in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger moths are a family of brightly patterned moths, so the answer names a winged invertebrate.

clue.text: Oscar winner Billy denied last Oscar

indicators.note: being denied the final item means the end letter is removed

parts.note: the film director Billy Wilder won several Oscars

explanation.surface: An Academy Award-winning director misses out on his final statuette.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'Oscar' looks like the award again, but it is the first name of a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright, so his first name stands for his surname by a convention of naming people.

clue.text: Poor Fats Waller needing removal of second cataract

indicators.note: something in poor shape is in a bad state, so the letters are put in a different order
removal takes something away, so the named letter goes

parts.note: the jazz pianist's name taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: The jazz pianist Fats Waller, sadly, needs an eye operation for a cataract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cataract' suggests the eye condition, but here it is the older sense of a large waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract in its original sense is a large, steep fall of water over a precipice.

clue.text: Chagall's back — hop it!

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: the painter's first name with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at a returning painter to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as 'has returned', but it reverses the painter Marc Chagall's first name with its possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal commands telling someone to leave at once; 'hop it' is British slang for go away.

clue.text: Italian city all-night party girl set up

parts.note: a rave is an all-night dance party

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up stands it on end, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl organises an all-night party in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' looks like organising the party, but it turns the girl's name upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is a city in northern Italy famous for its Byzantine mosaics.

clue.text: Impressive standing of sergeants' mess?

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the word taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The impressive status of the sergeants' mess, the dining hall for senior non-commissioned army ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: A sergeants' mess is the army dining room for sergeants, so 'mess' sits naturally in the phrase before it turns out to be the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatness is eminence or distinction, a lofty reputation or position in people's eyes.

clue.text: Monsieur is in Flanders port cycling farthest

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within
going round in a cycle moves letters from the front to the back

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur
Ostend is a Belgian port in Flanders

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is in the Belgian port of Ostend, cycling the greatest distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like a bike ride, but it moves OST from the front of the port's name to the back, and the Frenchman's abbreviation then goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means nearest the end, so it describes whatever is at the furthest extremity of a row.

clue.text: Reportedly forgo classes in electrical oscillation charts

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound is used rather than the spelling

parts.note: to waive is to forgo a right
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: Apparently someone skips lessons about electrical oscillation charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first part is a sound-alike. In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Waveforms are the plotted shapes of a signal over time, as shown on an oscilloscope, so they are graphs of electrical oscillations.

clue.text: Fine wildebeest served up on bed of porcini mushrooms

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest

indicators.note: a bed is what lies at the bottom, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the Italian mushroom

explanation.surface: A fine dish of wildebeest served on a bed of porcini mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' and 'bed of' read as menu language; in a down clue they reverse the animal and place the mushroom's last letter at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungi is the plural of fungus, the kingdom to which all mushrooms belong.

clue.text: Stormy regularly hosts party — a scene of utter depravity!

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one piece goes inside the other
at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A woman called Stormy often throws wild parties full of debauchery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' looks like a person's name or mood but only supplies alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom is the biblical city destroyed for its wickedness, now a byword for any place of vice.

clue.text: Beam technology unaffected by reflection

parts.note: surface reading: a system that sends out radio beams and detects their reflections
setter's reading: the word reads the same in a mirror order, back to front

explanation.surface: A beam-based detection system that is not thrown off by echoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that radar depends on reflection, yet the word itself is a palindrome, unchanged when reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar locates objects by bouncing radio beams off them, and its name is identical read forwards or backwards.

clue.text: Casually meet on Turin ground

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bumping into someone by chance at the football ground in Turin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' suggests a stadium in Turin, but it is the past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is an idiom for encountering them by chance.

clue.text: Top game covered by Media Bologna

indicators.note: something covered by other things is concealed beneath them, so the answer sits inside the words

parts.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: The Bologna press reports on a leading sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top game' reads as a leading match, but a top here is a spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling game with a two-cupped spinning top balanced on a string between two sticks.

clue.text: House leased in Aspen, it's amazing — it'll take some beating

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the phrase goes inside the rearranged letters
something amazing is bewildering, so the letters are thrown into confusion

parts.note: property leased is let
taken as written
a home is a house

explanation.surface: A rental house in the ski resort of Aspen is so amazing it will be hard to outdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It'll take some beating' is the idiom for something hard to surpass, but here the beating is of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish omelette is made from whisked eggs, so it literally needs a good amount of whisking before cooking.
